newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down, seen trying lower levels.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down, seen trying lower levels.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed down on Friday but off the day's low on late overseas selling, and dealers said prices would head lower.
Bullion hit a low of US$336.70/337.30 an ounce before ending at US$336.80/337.30, down from New York's US$338.00/50 close on Thursday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$337.80/338.30.
"Gold slipped in the afternoon session as the U.S. dollar racked up against the yen," said a dealer at a local investment house.
"The tone is a bit soft but there's a lack of trading interest with most local traders staying away ahead of the long holiday in Hong Kong."
The Hong Kong gold market will be closed Saturday through Wednesday for the public holiday marking the territory's return to Chinese rule on July 1.
Dealers saw gold dropping further in coming days but said physical demand and bargain-hunting at US$335-336 levels should provide support.
Local gold ended HK$10 lower at HK$3,120 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -6.00 from its previous fix at -8.00.
